Exercise 15.7.46 — Moment of Inertia of a Solid Cone About the z-Axis

Problem. Assume that the solid has constant density kkk. Find the moment of inertia about the zzz-axis of the solid cone x2+y2≤z≤h\sqrt{x^2+y^2} \le z \le hx2+y2​≤z≤h.

Notation used in this solution

SymbolMeaning
cone The solid with vertex at the origin and circular base of radius hhh in the plane z=hz=hz=h. A point is in the cone exactly when its height zzz is between its distance x2+y2\sqrt{x^2+y^2}x2+y2​ from the zzz-axis and hhh.
kkk The constant mass density.
IzI_zIz​ The moment of inertia about the zzz-axis: Iz=∭E(x2+y2) ρ dVI_z = \iiint_E (x^2+y^2)\,\rho\, dVIz​=∭E​(x2+y2)ρdV. The factor x2+y2x^2+y^2x2+y2 is the squared distance of a point from the zzz-axis.
(r,θ,z)(r,\theta,z)(r,θ,z) Cylindrical coordinates: x=rcos⁡θx = r\cos\thetax=rcosθ, y=rsin⁡θy = r\sin\thetay=rsinθ, x2+y2=r2x^2+y^2 = r^2x2+y2=r2, and dV=r dr dθ dzdV = r\,dr\,d\theta\,dzdV=rdrdθdz.

Part 1 — Set up and evaluate IzI_zIz​

Step 1.1: Describe the cone in cylindrical coordinates.

The inequality x2+y2≤z≤h\sqrt{x^2+y^2} \le z \le hx2+y2​≤z≤h becomes r≤z≤hr \le z \le hr≤z≤h. For the region to be nonempty we need 0≤r≤h0 \le r \le h0≤r≤h, and θ\thetaθ runs through a full turn. The solid is therefore

0≤θ≤2π,0≤r≤h,r≤z≤h. 0 \le \theta \le 2\pi, \qquad 0 \le r \le h, \qquad r \le z \le h. 0≤θ≤2π,0≤r≤h,r≤z≤h.

At height zzz the cross-section is the disk of radius zzz; the cone widens linearly from the vertex at the origin to its base of radius hhh at z=hz=hz=h.

Step 1.2: Write IzI_zIz​ as an iterated integral.

In cylindrical coordinates the squared distance from the zzz-axis is x2+y2=r2x^2+y^2 = r^2x2+y2=r2, and dV=r dr dθ dzdV = r\,dr\,d\theta\,dzdV=rdrdθdz. With the order dz dr dθdz\,dr\,d\thetadzdrdθ:

Iz=∫02π ⁣∫0h ⁣∫rhr2⋅r  dz dr dθ=k∫02π ⁣∫0h ⁣∫rhr3 dz dr dθ. I_z = \int_0^{2\pi}\!\int_0^{h}\!\int_r^{h} r^2 \cdot r\; dz\, dr\, d\theta = k\int_0^{2\pi}\!\int_0^{h}\!\int_r^{h} r^3\, dz\, dr\, d\theta. Iz​=∫02π​∫0h​∫rh​r2⋅rdzdrdθ=k∫02π​∫0h​∫rh​r3dzdrdθ.

Step 1.3: Evaluate the integrals.

∫rhr3 dz=r3(h−r)=hr3−r4, \int_r^{h} r^3\, dz = r^3 (h - r) = h r^3 - r^4, ∫rh​r3dz=r3(h−r)=hr3−r4, ∫0h(hr3−r4) dr=h⋅r44∣0h−r55∣0h=h54−h55=h520, \int_0^{h} (h r^3 - r^4)\, dr = h\cdot\frac{r^4}{4}\bigg|_0^{h} - \frac{r^5}{5}\bigg|_0^{h} = \frac{h^5}{4} - \frac{h^5}{5} = \frac{h^5}{20}, ∫0h​(hr3−r4)dr=h⋅4r4​​0h​−5r5​​0h​=4h5​−5h5​=20h5​, Iz=k∫02πh520 dθ=k⋅h520⋅2π=πkh510. I_z = k\int_0^{2\pi} \frac{h^5}{20}\, d\theta = k\cdot\frac{h^5}{20}\cdot 2\pi = \frac{\pi k h^5}{10}. Iz​=k∫02π​20h5​dθ=k⋅20h5​⋅2π=10πkh5​.

Result. Iz=πkh510. I_z = \frac{\pi k h^5}{10}. Iz​=10πkh5​.

Check against the standard formula. The cone has mass M=πkh33M = \tfrac{\pi k h^3}{3}M=3πkh3​ and base radius R=hR=hR=h. The standard moment of inertia of a solid cone about its symmetry axis is I=310MR2I = \tfrac{3}{10}MR^2I=103​MR2. Substituting gives 310⋅πkh33⋅h2=πkh510\tfrac{3}{10}\cdot\tfrac{\pi k h^3}{3}\cdot h^2 = \tfrac{\pi k h^5}{10}103​⋅3πkh3​⋅h2=10πkh5​, matching the result above.
